page.layout: One page of text, one column, with a running head at the top and the page number at the top left. No marginal notes. German words are set in black letter inside roman and italic text.

main_text.p: lina ac neutra: ut,der knab & knabe/puer, des knabe. der Herr & Herre/Dominus, des Herren. der Planet/ Planeta, des Planeten. das Herz/cor, des Herzen.

In e desinentia, si sint substantiæ, in singulari, No-minativum, Accusativum & Vocativum habent simi-les, in cæteris casibus, & in toto plurali assumunt n; Reliqua in e singulari numero sunt indeclinabilia: in plurali vero declinantur, sicut die laden. Fœmini-na in consonam desinentia, singulari numero sunt indeclinabilia: in plurali vero e assumunt, mutatis vocalibus ut supra, Dativo & Ablativo pluralibus n addunt: ut, die hand/ manus, die hende/ den henden. die brust/pectus: die brußte den brüsten. die Statt/ Urbs, die Stette/den Stetten.

head.i: Declina Adjectiva anomala, quæ Vulgò pronomina appellantur.

main_text.l: N. Ich / ego. G. meiner / mei. D. mihi / mihi.
A. mich / me. Abl. von mir / à me. Pluralis Num.
N. wir/ nos. G. unser / nostrum vel nostri. D. uns/ nobis. A. uns/nos. Abl. von uns / à nobis.
N. Du/ tu. G. deiner/ tui. D. dir/ tibi. A. dich/ te.
V. o du/ô tu. Abl. von dir / à te. Plur. Num. N. ihr/ vos. G. ewer / vestrum vel vestri. D. euch/ vobis. A. euch/vos. Voc. o ihr/ô vos. Abl. von euch / à vobis.
G. seiner/ihrer/seiner/sui. D. ihm/ihr/ihm/sibi. A. sich/se. Abl. von sich / à se. Plur. Num. G. ihrer/ sui. D. ihnen/sibi. A. sich/se. Abl. von sich/à se.
main_text.p: Ex dictis pronominibus oriuntur hæc possessiva: Mein/Dein/Sein.

page.notes: Several black-letter words are read with some doubt; I am not certain of the German spellings in the declension of "Sein" and in the "Abl." lines. Possible misreadings: "in e" (in the first paragraph, and "in e assumunt" in the second) and the sign "n" after "assumunt" and "pluralibus" may be printers' marks rather than letters. The line "die brußte den brüsten" is read as printed but may be a printing error. The first line is a fragment carried over from the previous page, with its opening cut off at the left edge. The last line is cut off at the lower right edge.
